scope: Follow-up on the s96-109 guideline review, structure only. Covers: the six quotation @source changes (yotzer_barukh_kevod, yotzer_qadosh and lael_asher_shavat, in HE and EN); the expanded-spine weekday and Shabbat Yotzer groups and their local j:declare elements; how the documentary El Adon continuation rubric is handled in expanded output; Bameh Madlikin moving to frankfurt_am_main; and whether each written decision holds up against JLPTEI-3.md. Checked against guideline-fixed-xml.xml, guideline-fix-resolutions.json, conditional-verification.json and schema/JLPTEI-3.md. I did not reopen source pointing, did not check transcription against the source, and did not accept any source.

findings.location: yotzer_qadosh.xml, yotzer_barukh_kevod.xml, lael_asher_shavat.xml (HE and EN): the occurrence-context tei:milestone[@unit='verse'] elements
findings.problem: These verse-unit milestones have @n set to a sub-verse label: 'qadosh', 'b', and 'a' on quoted_psalms_92_2. The Versification table in JLPTEI-3.md says a verse milestone's @n is the canonical verse number. The local corresp name quoted_psalms_92_2 also reads as the whole verse, while the bounded seg now points to 92/2/a. This does not affect alignment, because both languages carry the same corresp, and the canonical scope sits on seg/@source. Only display and labelling are inconsistent. The bundle does not show whether @n was changed in this round.
findings.fix: Optional, and safe to defer: in a later convention cleanup, give occurrence-context verse milestones the canonical verse number in @n (n='3', n='12', n='2'). The sub-verse precision stays in seg/@source. Leave the corresp identities as they are; no new identities are needed.

verified: All six @source changes appear in the bundle exactly as the resolutions list them, and they are the same in HE and EN: ezekiel/3/12 -> ezekiel/3/12/b, isaiah/6/3 -> isaiah/6/3/qadosh, psalms/92/2 -> psalms/92/2/a. The URN forms follow the Sub-verse scope rules: /b is a half-verse, /qadosh is a declared verse-part, and the names contain no '-'.

Each seg's wording covers what the new scope means. The HE Ezekiel seg is exactly Barukh…mimmeqomo, the second half-verse. The HE Psalm seg is exactly tov…ladonai (92:2a). The Isaiah seg starts at qadosh and runs to the end of the verse, which matches a verse-part that runs until the next verse milestone. Psalm 92:1 stays a whole-verse source, which is correct for מזמור שיר ליום השבת.

EN translations pointing at Hebrew sub-verse URNs in seg/@source is allowed. @source names the quoted canonical text, and translations not carrying half-verses only matters for resolving a project's own milestones.

Expanded Shabbat group: j:conditional with an HE/EN instruction note (shabbat=true), then an inner tei:div whose j:declare (shabbat=true) and j:endDeclare are siblings around the three transclusions. The weekday group has the same shape with shabbat=false and its own rubric. Both follow the j:declare sibling and containment rules and the 'Conditions on a running order' pattern of declaring a fixed feature value inside the gate. Because the declaration comes right after a conditional on the same feature, it is not gated a second time.

Using a condition rubric (On Shabbat / On a weekday) for the Yotzer alternatives fits 'Kinds of rubric'. It is a choice between passages inside a prayer that the reader must make, not a silent processor gate. It prints only when shabbat is undefined.

Documentary El Adon keeps the printed continuation rubric ('אַם שַׁבָּת.' / 'On Sabbath.') as the instruction note of el_adon_segment_2, with its tei:pb and page location intact. Under the expanded group's declare shabbat=true, that inner condition evaluates true, so the note is hidden per the conditional-note rule, including when the outer group's own condition is undefined. All four checks in conditional-verification.json report continued_page_rubric_settled=true, and the null-Shabbat case contains El Adon and Hakol. This matches the documentary_instruction_policy: the source evidence is kept, and expanded output never shows a mid-verse rubric.

The four compiler checks match the truth tables: (shabbat=null, ffm=false) keeps both alternatives and keeps Bameh with its rubric, since any(undef,false)=undef; (false,false) keeps only hameir and drops Bameh; (true,false) keeps only the Shabbat group and Bameh; (false,true) keeps hameir and Bameh. The conditional-verification.json payload is identical to resolutions.tests.

Bameh Madlikin conditions on j:any(holiday-aggregate/shabbat=true, rite/frankfurt_am_main=true). frankfurt_am_main is a separate binary rite feature, which the open rite feature set allows. Undefined behaves as described in the guideline: the passage is kept along with the Frankfurt instruction. The resolutions say the key now matches the later Frankfurt rules; I accept that from the resolutions and did not inspect those rules. The redundant j:all wrapper around a single j:any is harmless.

Decision on occurrence-context verse milestones: accepted as established repository convention per the cited test (test_repeated_scripture_has_addressable_chapter_and_verse_context). HE and EN carry the same unit and corresp, the canonical reference stays in the bounded seg/@source, and it is not an unregistered change. This also fits the guideline's 'do not duplicate a canonical URN merely because the text is printed again'.
Decision on Psalm 104:24: the XPath evidence shows exactly one canonical mapping per documentary project (yotzer_hameir.xml milestone[2] in both HE and EN), so the existing identity is kept.

Decision on bare chapter context markers: under rule 3, tei:milestone[@unit='chapter'] without corresp is a terminator that opens nothing, so these markers add no URN mapping and close no indexed scope. The bare verse terminators correctly close each occurrence-context verse scope before the following prose. No scope or alignment defect.
Bible sub-verse identities: Isaiah6:3/qadosh is declared in common/subverse.py, and WLC Ezekiel3:12/b and Ps92:2/a exist as stated in the request. No new identities are introduced.
limits: Structural decision only. This is not source acceptance: fine-mark review, transcription accuracy and source pointing stay separate and were not reopened.

I did not run the compiler, the schema validation or the importer tests myself. Compiler behaviour is taken from the supplied conditional-verification.json and resolutions payloads, and the subverse.py, WLC and test-file facts are taken as stated in the request.

I only reviewed the expanded-spine fragments in the bundle (weekday and Shabbat Yotzer groups, Bameh Madlikin). I did not check the rest of the expanded index or the later Frankfurt rules referred to as the precedent for frankfurt_am_main.
I did not check features.yaml for the frankfurt_am_main entry. The guideline treats the rite feature set as open.
